jobs.tierReason: live board responsiveness; Opus review in train 8
jobs.prompt:
FILE ACCESS: declared outputs are writable. Train 8 top priority: a board change (a job finishes, a run fails, something needs the owner) must show in the Command Center within a few seconds, not up to the 60 s snapshot cache TTL. Current behavior: one full board snapshot cached 60 s with stale-while-revalidate; the client polls every 5 s; a change after a build appears only after the next full rebuild (up to ~60 s + 5 s + 2.5 s). Do NOT shorten the cache to rebuild the whole snapshot often (that was the 44% CPU bug). Push changes through incrementally instead.

Design:
1) Cheap change detection on the server (tools/watch-server.mjs, with whatever helpers fit in tools/board-data.mjs or a new module): every ~1 s, stat the board's small input set (each project's .swarm/project/tickets.json and .swarm/orchestrator/events.ndjson, .swarm/runs/*/state.json, the inbox/lanes/history files used by the board) and compare mtime+size to a cache. On a change, identify the affected project id(s) without building the full snapshot.
2) Push: add a token/cookie-authenticated SSE endpoint for the Command Center (e.g. GET /api/command-center/events, same security headers, no token in logs) that sends a compact event when the inputs change: {kind:'cc-change', projects:[ids], at}. Keep the full 60 s snapshot cache for cold loads/consistency; on change, update the cached snapshot's affected project card and aggregate counters in place (build only the changed project(s), not all nine) so a later full request is current without a full rebuild.
3) Client (command-center-boot.js/cc-hive-mount.js): subscribe to the events (EventSource with the page cookie; pause on document.hidden), and on a cc-change event fetch only the changed project(s) via /api/command-center/project?id= (or apply the event's card data) and patch the Hive project card/cockpit and the header counters (needs-you, done 24h) in place. Do not rebuild the DOM or the full snapshot. Keep the 5 s poll as a slower fallback; if the SSE drops, fall back to polling. Honor the reduced-motion/visibility behavior.
4) Latency target: a ticket/run/inbox change is visible within 3 s. Add tests: a fixture board with a project; change a tickets.json and an inbox/state file; assert the event fires within ~1 s, names the right project, the cached full snapshot updates only that project when requested, and the client patch path runs without a full snapshot fetch. Test the SSE token/auth + security headers, and that no token appears in logs/URLs. Keep all existing command-center/watch-server/perf tests green.
Verify: node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/command-center-live.test.mjs tests/watch-server.test.mjs tests/watch-token-urls.test.mjs tests/command-center-routes-flag.test.mjs tests/command-center-boot.test.mjs tests/command-center-perf-budget.test.mjs -> all pass. Report the detected latency and the design.
